US-532 CLOSED + COMMITTED as 6a4af44 (Sprint 71 / V0.29.26, 3/6 done). NO TD-059 STALL -- gate ran synchronously in-loop, then COMMIT, then bookkeeping. NEXT: US-533 (wire the 5 settings end-to-end) or US-536 (disposition-B revert, size S). Read the Atlas --disable-gpu RCA inbox item BEFORE US-536.

WHAT SHIPPED: Iris Option B -- a Settings band at the TOP of the EXISTING US-403 setup-menu overlay, above OBD-II Services. No 5th carousel card. A toggle is a 2-choice segment (Off/On), power mode a 3-choice one (CAR/WALL/UNKNOWN) -- ONE render mechanism for both, and 'unknown' is expressible as NO choice selected, which is how an unreadable setting shows itself instead of defaulting to a confident Off.

*** THE DESIGN CALL: PER-REQUEST, NOT CACHED -- AND THE CODEBASE ALREADY HELD BOTH ANSWERS. *** carouselConfig is resolved ONCE at handler construction (US-506); __DEPLOY_VERSION__ is resolved PER REQUEST (US-501, whose comment says it had to move because a startup-cached value is always one deploy stale). The settings band has US-501's failure mode exactly: save autoRotateS=0 -> reload the page without bouncing the unit -> a cached blob renders 8 again, silently discarding a save that DID happen. Mutation B (cache at construction) -> EXACTLY 1 red, the freshness test, confirming its own docstring's claim that every other test in the file passes against the cached version. GENERAL LESSON: when a codebase contains two patterns for 'when do I resolve this?', they are not interchangeable styles -- one of them has a comment explaining a bug. Go read that comment before picking.

I DELIBERATELY DID NOT FORCE PARITY WITH DISPLAY_CAROUSEL, AND THIS IS THE PART I'D HAVE GOT WRONG ON INSTINCT. After a save-without-bounce, DISPLAY_SETTINGS.autoRotateS (stored: 0) and DISPLAY_CAROUSEL.autoRotateS (running: 8) DISAGREE. US-530's lesson is 'assert the AGREEMENT when N consumers must agree on one fact' -- so my reflex was a parity test. WRONG HERE: they are not the same fact. One is what is STORED, one is what is RUNNING (cached at states-http startup, Atlas GAP 1). A parity assertion would have forced the band to report the stale running value -- i.e. to HIDE the gap. The 'applies on restart' label is what makes the gap honest. Know which fact a test is pinning before you pin two things to each other.

APPLY-STATE LABELS SHIP CONSERVATIVE ON ALL 5 ROWS -- A DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM IRIS'S TABLE, READ BEFORE US-533. She specced power mode / audio alerts 'live' and triggerAfterDrive 'next drive'. But an apply-state is a CLAIM ABOUT A CONSUMER and US-532 wires NO consumer (that IS US-533's acceptance). A restart always applies an overlay value, so 'applies on restart' can never be a lie; 'applies now' would be an over-promise, and over-promising is the DANGEROUS direction -- it is precisely the silent no-op this band exists to prevent. Under-promising costs a needless restart. The note is DERIVED from one {live,restart,next-drive} mapping, so US-533 flips `apply` per key and test_noRowClaimsLiveUntilItsConsumerIsWired goes red ON PURPOSE. That red is the handshake, not a regression.

*** HONEST BOUND -- THE ONE THING I COULD NOT PROVE. *** Mutation A (repaint from the REQUEST instead of the server's re-read) was caught by SOURCE INSPECTION ONLY. Every pure non-echo test stayed GREEN, because they exercise settingsSaveResult in isolation and the DOM is free to ignore its answer. There is no DOM harness in this kit -- carousel_probe.js evaluates pure exports with no document -- so EVERY 'the wiring actually applies the policy' guard here is a source-text assertion (the same ceiling US-490 hit). The reducer is provably honest; that the DOM USES it is textual. US-533's live Pi round-trip is what closes this.

ONE PAINT PATH PER ROW: a single `render` closure, built once per row, used for the initial paint AND handed to the save handler. Stronger than two call sites agreeing -- if the save handler painted the row itself it could paint the requested value while the open path paints the stored one, and the UI would disagree with ITSELF across a reload.

CROSS-LANGUAGE SSOT GUARD (strictly stronger than US-531's bound): the display MUST carry its own key list (different runtime, cannot import the Python allow-list), so the risk is DRIFT not duplication. The JS list is pinned to overlay.OVERRIDABLE_KEYS in BOTH directions including order, and the row/write tests are parametrized over the Python SSOT. Mutation D (drift one key) -> 4 red. This is the guard US-531 could not build, because there a currently-identical local copy still passed.

MUTATIONS (all 5 reverted BY HAND -- git checkout is outside the allow-list -- and re-verified green): (A) echo the request -> 1 red (source-inspection only, see bound above). (B) cache at construction -> 1 red. (C) truthy bool coercion hides unknown -> 3 red. (D) key drift -> 4 red. (E) drop X-Splash-Token -> 1 red.

NO GET /settings, per US-531's ruling -- the injection already carries the fact, and a read route would be a second source that could disagree. NO confirm on the toggles: they are reversible, and borrowing the service confirm would train the operator to dismiss the modal guarding a service Stop.

REAL-CONFIG SMOKE (against a COPY of the shipped config.json in tmp -- repo tree never written): injected effective = 8/unknown/false/false/true, keys == allow-list; POST autoRotateS=0 + power.mode=wall both 200; RE-SERVED with NO restart -> band showed 0 + wall (per-request property proven live); UNAUTHED -> 401 AND overlay still 'wall' afterwards (absence of a side effect, not just a status code); pi.obd.port -> 403; 'moon-base' -> 400; config.json BYTE-UNCHANGED; tmp removed.

GATE: RED first for the right reason (ImportError: cannot import name 'loadEffectiveSettings'). Then 64 story tests green + the whole tests/ui/ suite (551) + tests/pi/splash/ + tests/common/test_config_overlay*.py + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py. 1 skip, PRE-EXISTING (test_token.py:70 POSIX file-mode on Windows). ruff clean on 3 .py files; validate_config.py passes.

BLAST RADIUS FOR PM: strictly ADDITIVE -- git diff --numstat shows 0 DELETIONS across all 4 source files. No existing route/export/CSS rule modified. The only behavioural change to existing code is openMenu() also calling buildSettings(). Full suite still warranted at integration (states_http_server is on the Pi serve path).

LIVE VALIDATION OWED: the band is proven through the real HTTP server + real config.json on the dev box, NOT on the Pi through the kiosk's chromium. Needs deploy + eclipse-states-http bounce. Whoever validates: the kebab is PARKED-ONLY (US-490) -- on a driving Pi use the 5s long-press.

ENVIRONMENT: `make` still NOT on PATH (exits 127, READS LIKE A PASS) -- use `python -m ruff check` per file (TD-075). Bash still rejects heredocs with brace-with-quote -- use dict() / dict([(k,v)]).
